The USB-C PD stage regulates the output voltage to the selected PD level. It is supplied from the secondary bulk capacitor, which is charged by the resonant converter. Changes in current drawn from the USB-C output therefore affect the bulk voltage regulated by the MCU.

The resonant stage supplies the secondary bulk bus upstream of the MPQ4242 output regulator. Fixed VBUS settings of \SI{5}{\volt}, \SI{9}{\volt}, \SI{15}{\volt}, and \SI{20}{\volt} were tested. Bulk-voltage feedback enters the MCU at PA1; the connector-voltage measurements are downstream of this control loop.

Fixed VBUS settings of \SI{5}{\volt}, \SI{9}{\volt}, \SI{15}{\volt}, and \SI{20}{\volt} were tested. Connector voltage was measured downstream of the bulk-voltage control loop.

The PCB was designed and assembled for this project. The supplied inductor and transformer were integrated, and the power, auxiliary, sensing, and output-interface circuits were implemented. The MCU firmware was developed in stages, from open-loop bring-up to the DMA-based voltage controller, with startup sequencing, bounded burst control, load classification, no-load operation, and overvoltage inhibition.

The firmware was then adapted for the MCU on V2. The revised board integrates the control, isolated feedback, local supplies, and USB-C output with the power stage. Browser control and logging were added, and the resonant tank was modified during powered testing. The schematic and PCB documentation are included in Appendix~\ref{app:hardware}.

Firmware development began with open-loop bring-up and progressed to DMA-based voltage control. Startup sequencing, bounded burst control, load classification, no-load operation, and overvoltage inhibition were added to manage the operating states.

For V2, the firmware was adapted to the onboard MCU, and control, isolated feedback, local supplies, and USB-C output were integrated with the power stage. Browser control and logging were added. During powered testing, the resonant tank was modified after the series inductor became hot. The schematic and PCB documentation are included in Appendix~\ref{app:hardware}.

Three time scales govern operation: carrier-scale phase, clamp timing, and energy per active cycle; burst-scale average transfer; and line-cycle storage imbalance in the DC link and secondary capacitors. The model must resolve all three time scales.

Nominal series resonance is near \SI{0.989}{\mega\hertz}. Turn-on phase also depends on magnetizing current, pump current, and rectifier state, which must be included in commutation prediction.

Calibration requires matched input and secondary demand, followed by separate comparisons of voltage envelopes and switching waveforms. Mean VBUS agreement alone does not validate bulk ripple or commutation current. Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports these quantities separately.
new:
The model must resolve carrier-scale phase, clamp timing, and energy per active cycle, as well as average transfer over each burst and the line-cycle energy imbalance in the DC link and secondary capacitors. Nominal series resonance is near \SI{0.989}{\mega\hertz}, but turn-on phase also depends on magnetizing current, pump current, and rectifier state.

Calibration requires matched input and secondary demand, followed by separate comparisons of voltage envelopes and switching waveforms. This checks bulk ripple and commutation current as well as mean VBUS. Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports these quantities separately.

final_new:

Calibration requires matched input and secondary demand, followed by separate comparisons of voltage envelopes and switching waveforms. Both comparisons are needed to assess bulk ripple and commutation current as well as mean VBUS. Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports these quantities separately.

The no-load guard uses the primary-current indication at PA2 and the configured reference conditions to select a narrower band and lower high-duty cap. The defaults are \(V_{\mathrm{set}}=\SI{28}{\volt}\), \(V_{\mathrm{NLdrop}}=\SI{5}{\volt}\), and \(d_{\mathrm{NL}}=\SI{5}{\percent}\), giving approximately \SI{23}{\volt} to \SI{28}{\volt} at the secondary bulk. These defaults apply to the secondary bulk supply; the USB-C output has its own voltage setting.
